bphs-97:santhanam:ch04:v25-30.exact_text: 25-30. Nishek Lagn. O excellent of Brahmins, now is a step explained to arrive at the Nishek Lagna, when the natal Lagn is known. Note the angular distance between Shani and Mandi (Gulik). Add this to the difference between the Lagn Bhava (Madhya, or cusp) and the 9<sup>th</sup> Bhava (cusp). The resultant product in Rāśis, degrees etc. will represent the months, days etc., that elapsed between Nishek and birth. At birth, if Lagn Lord is in the invisible half (i.e. from Lagn cusp to descendental cusp), add the degrees etc., Chandra moved in the particular Rāśi, occupied by her, to the above-mentioned product. Then Lagn at Nishek can be worked out and the good and bad, experienced by the native in the womb, can be guessed. One can also guess with the help of Nishek Lagn effects, like longevity, death etc. of the parents.
